claims.text: Wear performance of high-entropy-alloy protective coatings is governed by formation of a stable nanocrystalline oxide layer at the wear surface.
The nanocrystalline oxide layer acts as a barrier to abrasive wear.
The nanocrystalline oxide layer reduces the coefficient of friction.
Changing coating composition or microstructure can alter the formation and stability of the nanocrystalline oxide layer.
Formation of a stable nanocrystalline oxide layer improves wear resistance.
Formation of a stable nanocrystalline oxide layer lowers the coefficient of friction.
The proposed baseline is a high-entropy-alloy coating that does not form a nanocrystalline oxide layer.
The hypothesis is intended to apply only to coatings with suitable composition and microstructure and to loads and speeds within an unspecified range.
XPS and TEM can be used to characterize the composition and microstructure of the worn surface.
Failure of wear performance to improve when a stable nanocrystalline oxide layer forms would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe a nanocrystalline oxide layer at the wear surface would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is explicitly defined as a coating without a nanocrystalline oxide layer, while the falsification rule states that failure to observe such a layer falsifies the hypothesis. Thus, the expected baseline observation would itself satisfy part of the stated falsification rule.
